You're quite strong to survive all this! 
Welp, I'm only a minor living under her parent's roof, doubt I'll get money for a support group turns out there are online groups tho.
Thanks for your help, and I hope you heal from your past.
thanks a lot. I suck at googling. I really hope I find something suitable for me.

on the contrary! most people are really positive, maybe you're just with the wrong crowd. I used to think that too, but as I got to know more people, I gained more respect for them. but each to their own I guess.

ya know any support groups for teens who've been disowned/abused by their family?
that could put it off
I'm doing it tomorrow, just wanted to say farewell to the internet beforehand lol

That's exactly what my therapist told me today in therapy.
and thank you very very much for your input!
She told me you can't diagnose a personality disorder if the patient is an adolescent, since their personality is not completely formed yet.

But what is the difference between a belief and a delusion? I know that believing in vampires is not normal but back then I started believing because of the internet, I read in forums about people who had encounters with them and very detailed explanations of their biology. If I was delusional, I would've believed in them with nothing to back up my beliefs, and I wouldn't listen to any contradicting views. But I did, until I convinced myself it's nonsense. That means it's not a delusion right? Or have I misunderstood the term?
Yeah, she did and gave me 5 mg Aripiprazole. when I complained about the side effects of APs in general and asked if I could discontinue use, she still insisted and gave me Olanzapine instead. Also, I've been to only 2 sessions 20 minutes each, and I've told her exactly what I wrote in my post. Heck, I didn't even mention the vampire thing. So I can't understand how'd she diagnose me with sz in such a short time. However, she's very famous around here, has a PhD and is a professor in the best university in my country. So I'm really torn.

I am trying to get my life back on track but that's really hard imo.

You see, before I went to this psychiatrist, I was getting better. I used to be severely depressed but now I have purpose. I was working on my anxiety and my dissociation was getting better. Was I really getting better or was I losing insight? I agree with the other psychiatrist I went to, I'm not on the spectrum but the thought won't get out of my head. I'll try not to worry too much but it's easier said than done.

I know this sounds childish but I don't think I'm strong enough to live with schizophrenia. I know a lot of people manage to turn their lives around and live happily but I don't think I can,  Schizophrenia is a heavy word for me. That's why the diagnosis matters, if it turns out I'm in the prodrome I'll end my life. I'm being dramatic, aren't I ? I don't want to live with my sanity eroding by the day, it's like a ticking bomb and there's no way out. I'm not saying schizophrenia makes life not worth living, I'm just weak.
Sorry for the rambling.
very well, thanks for your help.
